title: Unconventional Spin Valve Based on Normal Metal/Chiral Molecule/Altermagnet Junctions
authors: Tian-Yi Zhang, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, Ai-Min Guo, Qing-Feng Sun
abstract: Chiral molecules have attracted broad interdisciplinary interest for their ability to produce highly spin-polarized current. This phenomenon, known as the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect, holds great potential in the field of spintronics. Here, we propose to combine chiral molecules with altermagnets to construct highly efficient and tunable spin valves. Using the nonequilibrium Green's function method and the Landauer-Büttiker formula, we obtain the conductance and the magnetoresistance of a normal metal/chiral molecule/altermagnet spin valve. Our theoretical results reveal that the conductance of the spin valve can be effectively tuned by reorienting the Néel vector of the altermagnet, and the magnetoresistance of the spin valve increases with molecular length and altermagnetic anisotropy. Moreover, the magnetoresistance vanishes for achiral molecules or in the absence of molecular spin-orbit coupling. Our work paves the way for developing efficient, controllable, and stray-field-free spintronic devices.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates a novel spintronic device—a spin valve built from a normal metal, a chiral molecule, and an altermagnet. By calculating the conductance and magnetoresistance using Green's functions, the authors demonstrate that chirality and the AM's unique magnetic properties synergistically enhance the MR effect. This paves the way for building controllable, stray-field-free spintronic devices.
main_problem: The research aims to develop highly efficient and tunable spin valves by integrating chiral molecules with altermagnetic (AM) materials, aiming to surpass limitations of conventional ferromagnetic spin valves.
main_result: The theoretical model predicts that the magnetoresistance (MR) is significantly enhanced by combining chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) in the molecule with the momentum-dependent spin splitting inherent to the AM electrode. This MR increases with molecular length and AM anisotropy.
method: The study employs non-equilibrium Green's function methods combined with the Landauer-Büttiker formula to calculate transport properties across the junction.
model_or_system: The physical system modeled is a Normal Metal/Chiral Molecule/Altermagnet (NM/chiral molecule/AM) spin valve. The Hamiltonian incorporates terms for the AM, NM, chiral molecule (single-helical model), and coupling interactions.
key_observables: Conductance ($G$) and Magnetoresistance ($	ext{MR}$), which are calculated as a function of external parameters like Néel vector orientation ($	heta$) and molecular length ($N_z$).
important_parameters: Chiral molecule twist angle ($\Delta\varphi$), AM anisotropy, dephasing strength ($\Gamma_d$), and the relative alignment of the AM's Néel vector ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The model includes a dephasing term ($H_d$) to account for real-world scattering effects, and it assumes the CISS effect is active due to molecular chirality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the junction structure, show Fermi surfaces in the AM depending on spin and orientation ($	heta$), and plot conductance/MR dependence on $	heta$, $\alpha$, and molecule length ($N_z$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model (Hamiltonian), details the theoretical methodology (NEGF/Landauer-Büttiker), presents results showing how MR arises from the interplay of chirality and AM properties, and concludes by discussing device potential.
why_interesting: This work connects molecular electronics (CISS effect) with advanced magnetic materials (Altermagnets) to engineer spin transport phenomena using purely theoretical quantum transport methods, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems dynamics in condensed matter.
